**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-20**
- **Member:** Avery Alvarez
- **Member ID:** W460125797
- **Reference number:** POC-55381BDBC3-44861
- **Service denied:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
- **Governing policy:** *Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O)*, effective July 1, 2026 — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which UnitedHealthcare Community Plan denied on August 20, 2026. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already gathered for the prior authorization request describe my condition, my treatment history, and my imaging in detail. I am setting that information out again below, organized against the plan's own policy.

## The plan's policy does not exclude this surgery — it points to criteria the plan holds

The policy that governs my request, *Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O)*, begins with this statement:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

So ankle surgery is not excluded under my plan. The policy then explains where the detailed standards live:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

and it identifies the applicable subsets, including the one that covers my procedure:

> "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

The policy also confirms that the plan relies on this outside tool:

> "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits."

I want to be straightforward with you about what I can and cannot see. The excerpt above ends in a colon and points to a list of clinical conditions in the InterQual Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle subset that is not reproduced in the portion of the policy available to me. I am therefore **not quoting any specific numeric threshold, required duration, number of visits, or imaging grade as the plan's requirement**, because the policy text I have does not state one. The plan has not told me what standard my records were measured against. The facts below are simply my facts, as my chart records them.

## What my records document

| What the records show | Source in the prior authorization packet |
|---|---|
| Twelve months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest | Clinical summary |
| Supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance — 10 weeks, 2026-05-15 through 2026-07-24, 16 visits completed | Physical therapy discharge note |
| NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief | Medication history |
| Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29, which gave three weeks of partial relief | Medication/injection history |
| Weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-07-12 showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts | Imaging report |
| Antalgic gait; walking limited to two blocks | Functional assessment |
| Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain | Physical exam |
| No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker | Clinical summary |
| Total ankle replacement documented as needed by Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery | Surgeon's documentation |

In plain terms: I have tried rest, months of anti-inflammatory medication, a steroid injection, and a full supervised course of physical therapy. None of it gave me lasting relief. My weight-bearing X-rays show that the joint space in my tibiotalar joint is gone and that there are subchondral cysts. I cannot walk more than two blocks. I also do not have the conditions that commonly rule a person out of joint replacement — no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I do not smoke.

## One part of the policy does not apply to my request

The policy contains this statement:

> "Osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant is unproven and not medically necessary for treating cartilage defects of the ankle due to insufficient evidence of efficacy."

The policy's supporting discussion of that technology includes the observations that

> "All studies exhibited a high risk of bias in at least one domain, with 64% demonstrating a high risk across at least four domains."

and

> "however, a considerable number of the allografts failed, requiring repeat allografting, arthrodesis, or arthroplasty (range, 11%-48%)."

It also notes:

> "Clinical Practice Guidelines American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) The AOFAS (2022) published a position statement that supports the use of osteochondral autograft and allograft transplant for the treatment of OLTs that have failed nonsurgical management, especially for large-diameter lesions, cystic lesions, and lesions that have failed previous surgical treatment."

I am raising these only to be clear that they are not about my case. I am not requesting an osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant. I am requesting a total ankle replacement, CPT 27702 — a procedure the policy routes to the InterQual "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle" subset named above. If any part of the review of my request relied on the unproven-technology language, I ask that it be set aside and my request be reviewed under the criteria that actually apply to a total ankle replacement.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

I am asking the plan, in writing, to provide **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with any internal guideline or clinical rationale the reviewer relied on. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must give me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion it relied on in denying my claim. The plan holds this material; I do not. Because InterQual is licensed software rather than a public document, I cannot read it, and I cannot know which element of it my records were found to be missing.

This matters directly to the reason given for the denial. The policy itself states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I accept that documentation may be required and that submitting it does not by itself guarantee coverage. But if the determination was that my documentation was incomplete, I am asking the plan to identify specifically **which document or clinical finding it considers missing**, so that Dr. Reyes and I can supply it. I will provide any additional record the plan identifies, promptly and without argument. Without that specific list, neither my surgeon nor I can respond to the stated reason.

## What I am asking for

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-20 (reference POC-55381BDBC3-44861) and authorize total ankle replacement, CPT 27702.
2. If the denial is not overturned, identify in writing the exact InterQual subset, edition, and criteria text applied, and the specific documentation element found to be missing.
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery experience, and confirm in writing the reviewer's specialty.

I am filing this appeal within the period stated in my denial notice. The notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by February 16, 2027**. I am submitting it through the appeal channel identified for my plan — by signing in at **member.uhc.com** and filing the appeal there, and/or by mailing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I may also call the number on my member ID card. My denial letter is the authoritative source for the address and the deadline, and I am using the address printed on it.

Please also treat this letter as my request to receive copies of all documents, records, and criteria relevant to this claim.

Thank you for taking a careful second look. My surgeon has documented that this operation is needed, and I would like to get back to walking further than two blocks.

Sincerely,

**Avery Alvarez**
